title: D-087 PLAN-1: the wiring plan for CAD/3D export and the 3D viewer - one design note that turns the accepted, unwired D-087 building blocks into an ordered, parallel-safe packet sequence (docs only)
objective: Write docs/design/d087-export-and-3d-viewer-plan.md: the design the orchestrator will contract the next D-087 packets from. (1) Inventory every accepted, unwired D-087 block with its public API and limits (app/cad dxf_writer / pdf_sheet_writer / glb_writer, app/drawings dxf_reader / sheet_reader, app/scenario massing_model, app/connectors building_footprints_arcgis) and map the open riders (DB-053..DB-062) to the step that must close each. (2) Propose the API contract for export (DXF, PDF site plan, GLB) and for a 3D scene payload (massing + lot + context buildings): flag-gating, request bounds, response types and Content-Disposition, size caps, time budgets, typed refusals, provenance and the honesty labels, logging with server-generated correlation ids, escaping of source text. (3) Design the web 3D viewer on the admitted three 0.186.0 + @react-three/fiber 9.7.0: data path, coordinate frames (EPSG:2263 feet -> local metres), performance limits, a non-visual text alternative, print behaviour, the @types/three decision laid out for the owner (package with its WASM physics dependency vs a reviewed local declaration file), and CI-only web testing. (4) The AutoCAD round trip: what importing an architect's DXF into the proposal editor would mean and what stays later. (5) An ordered packet breakdown with allowed paths, dependencies, gates, the riders each closes, and a disjointness plan for parallel builders. (6) The owner decisions still open (R008 DXF middleman confirmation, R007 DWG licensing, @types/three, real architect PDFs).
business_reason: The owner asked for 3D handling of buildings and lots and for AutoCAD import/export (D-087-R003/R004/R006); the building blocks are accepted but unwired, and a reviewed plan lets several builders wire them in parallel without colliding or skipping a safety rider.
